First sk—that it is built like a pot: Rashi’s wording.
“On its mouth,” etc., above: the Tur’s wording, because we learned “they even return.”
“And there is in it”: Shabbat 37b.
“That it is pomace”: the Tur’s wording; so too the Rambam in his commentary.
“To leave it on it unless”: like Rabba there after the entire sugya—it implies he is the conclusion of our passage.
“Or that it is raw”: Shabbat 18b.
“But if”: there [in the Gemara].
“And even if it finished cooking”: there 37b, in Rabba’s words.
“We are concerned”: there 18b; “now therefore,” etc.
“Unless”: Mishnah 36b.
“That he removed,” etc.: Yerushalmi.
“That is,” etc., “to exclude”: there in Yerushalmi; and in the Gemara 37a, “coals that dimmed,” etc.
“Two stoves”: there in the sugya of leaning.
“Even to lean”: there Abaye, and a baraisa supports him.
“And even if”: like Rav Ada’s reading; surely the Mishnah follows Rav Ada since it does not say “perhaps,” implying it is the sugya’s conclusion—yet halacha follows Abaye because of the baraisa.

“So too where the hand” recoils: there 40b—water and oil, etc.; how much more so a kirah; see Raavad Shabbat ch. 10—why here vs. above we forbade placing on a kirah—and see Yerushalmi “permitted to thaw in a place,” etc., and likewise Yerushalmi here.
“And how much more”: there Mishnah and baraisa.
“That it is a place”: there in the Gemara.
“If heated”: Mishnah there.
“And ovens”: Bava Batra 20b.

“And if he forgot and left”: there the second issue; the Rif explains unintentionally and when it improves beautifully; Tosafos there s.v. transgressed—and Rashi if the decree applies even when it improves beautifully; likewise implied there regarding eggs—see—and he rules leniently.
“And if”: there the first issue.
“And if he transgressed”: like Rabbi Yehuda there.
“Until kedei sheyeasu”: there 18b.

If a non-Jew returned the pots: deliberate action by a non-Jew for an Israelite’s need parallels unintentional action by an Israelite—for Israelites we rule like Rabbi Yehuda in Bava Kamma 71a that deliberate violation forbids the food permanently; in the Diaspora it is permitted within kedei sheyeasu, as Shabbat 151a and Beitzah 24b.

If [an Israelite] returned them: meaning even unintentionally it is forbidden if the dish improves beautifully, because “return” when it improves is treated like incomplete cooking for shehiyah—even Chananya, who permits ben drusai for shehiyah, forbids “return” permanently, as explained below.

If it shrinks and is harmed: meaning even though ab initio it is forbidden as the Ran derives from Shabbat 37b—and Rabbi Oshaya—and “hot water shrinks and harms,” as sk 1; see Tosafos 36b s.v. hot water regarding Beit Shammai.
It is permitted—for there Shabbat 18b they permit within kedei sheyeasu even if it cooked under prohibition, since one does not benefit.

“Some say that all…”: Shabbat 37b—Chananya and the plain sugya in ch. 3 follow him; we stretched to establish the Mishnah according to him; see Tosafos s.v. “always”; Rabbi Shimon citing Rabbi Yochanan with Rava’s support; both sources “are taught” and we resolve the Mishnah’s inference; Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda except teaches “if it improves beautifully” permitted per Rav Hai Gaon—great teaching—even though a decree could apply, stirring adds little so attention leads to stirring; proof Rav forbids “improves beautifully” yet permits ben drusai; ch. 3 Rav says “until ben drusai” though Rav and Shmuel dispute Rabbi Yochanan—halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan against them as the Rif writes; Rav Ukva from Mata told Rabbi Elazar “you near vs. we”—practice differs; Rabbeinu Tam’s story Magen Avraham end Shabbat; first approach: Gemara’s conclusion “like Rabba” settles it—all the more so incomplete cooking; Rashba challenged Chananya’s plain wording “anything cooked ben drusai”; ch. 3 sugya no proof since all agree per Ran; proofs involving Rav, Rava/Rav Sheshet, Rif; Rabbi Yochanan vs Rav/Shmuel; “one vs. two” does not apply.

“Or even…”: no distinction between oven and kirah except what an unstoked kirah forbids out of stirring concern is forbidden in an oven even if raked—as Shabbat 37b regarding kupach, except leaning; otherwise the Gemara’s question there fails—see Raavad; regarding shehiyah oven equals kirah for Rif and this reasoning—as ch. 3 raw pot in oven ben drusai—and all explain the Gemara.
“And it was not mentioned”: among codifiers—for the Mishnah was cited only regarding return, as there.

“And if he forgot,” etc., forbidden—Shabbat 37a; implies even for others, unlike Gemara on penalties for others; Rashi and Tosafos: Rabbi Meir deliberate vs Rabbi Yehuda unintentional—deliberate forbidden for others too.
“How much more so”: there.
“And all this regarding the matter”: as siman 257 sk 7—see there.
“And some say even…”: Tosafos beginning ch. 4 47b s.v. with what; Ritva distinguishes—see there.
“Only they are careful”: Shabbat 35b “one who removes,” etc.—according to Rif when it improves beautifully; others require another reason.
“Remove it from there”: definite pesik reisha via non-Jew permitted—as Magen Avraham sk 5 explains.

“Take care when taking it”: even without intent—pesik reisha forbidden; Kerisus 20b Tosafos; here rabbinic liability so permit via non-Jew as mere shvus Tevuos Shor; end of siman practice non-Jews remove pots; Tosafos as cited; if not taken gently pesik reisha—unlike Or Zarua siman 312 ch. 18; stirring coals—no prohibition from tiltul min ha-tsad—Mordechai; Magen Avraham 323 sk 1; Rashba s.v. if uncovered—even lenient opinion permits.
Second sk—as long as it boils: even though “no cooking after cooking,” since one may return when cooled there is [new] cooking—Shabbat 37d decree lest he boil it; Raavad ch. 3 sk 10.
“Still in his hand”: the uncertainties there were resolved stringently—Raavad.

“And he did not place it on the ground”: Rambam’s wording; the uncertainty resolved leniently following Yerushalmi as his custom; Yerushalmi there: placed on earth—moving forbidden… on a peg if still hot permitted; Rabbi Yochanan: unless he removed his hand—implies Magen Avraham’s view.

“His intent”: there the first version is stringent; Raavad ch. 4 sk 2 Rabbi Chanina: Shabbat severity like Torah; Rambam and Shulchan Aruch omitted Abaye—they followed Yerushalmi which did not cite Abaye.
Specifically: Rambam from Shabbat 18b lest stir—and even if boiling; Raavad ch. 3 sk 10 wrote until ben drusai—see siman 318.
Then permitted—Yerushalmi.
But—as above.
Some say—likewise Yerushalmi—see Ran.
Some say—Yerushalmi end of ch. “With what may we insulate”—see Rambam.
Some say all—Tosafos Shabbat 36b s.v. Beit Hillel: from “even on Shabbat” infer even on weekday they dispute; hence Beit Hillel regarding unstoked kirah.
For Barchu that it is: according to Tosafos and Rosh in siman 263 sk 10—its law is like nightfall, as siman 261 sk 4—see there.
If it is near: Tosafos there—see there.

His law is like on Shabbat itself—not literally, but it is forbidden on an unstoked kirah; on a stoked one all permit, with no difference between having placed on the ground or still in hand—Raavad there; though in ch. 4 he did not write so, there he copied Tosafos’ language as usual, but in his own view it is permitted as above. Support from Yerushalmi there: if removed by day return by day; from dark return from dark; removed erev Shabbat and day sanctified—placed on earth forbidden—but with those permitted universally; Ran permits erev Shabbat until dark.

Some are lenient—Ran: cannot derive from Beit Shammai to Beit Hillel since Beit Shammai holds whatever forbidden on Shabbat forbidden erev Shabbat Shabbat 17b Mishnah—and “even on Shabbat” implies both forbid Shabbat but dispute erev Shabbat—each follows his reasoning as above.
But to lean—there Shabbat 37a—see Tosafos s.v. what.
Even near fire… even near—meaning even though on Shabbat nearby fire is forbidden per Tosafos s.v. indeed—even erev Shabbat near nightfall it is permitted thus even for those who forbid.
And [similarly] regarding an oven—as above sk 1.
Specifically—as there.
Third sk—an old [pot]: Beitzah 34a.
Empty—because of the pot itself [without food].
Against the mouth of the kirah—Magen Avraham.
Take care… already—as explained sk 2.
Fourth sk—there is—Rema and Magen Avraham.

Fifth sk—permitted to place… because this is not the normal way of cooking—according to siman 318 sk 15 Magen Avraham; some are lenient—the Rashba’s view as in his novellae: not forbidden opposite bonfire or first vessel unless cold and uncooked; decree lest thaw equals decree lest cook—but cold cooked food even first vessel or opposite fire—even yad soledes permitted—provided not directly on coals or kirah. We say whatever entered hot… although derivative of fire is fire liable chatos ch.3 wheel liable; oil—even yad soledes permitted—hold oil has no “cooking”; salt—even first vessel permitted—not cooked in first vessel; hence even uncooked hard meat permitted first vessel/bonfire/yad soledes. Rule: wherever no cooking will occur—or no cooking prohibition—or cannot cook—permitted first vessel or bonfire—even though return forbidden unstoked and placing initially forbidden even stoked even hot fully cooked—there reason appearance of cooking usual path; on fire directly—but first vessel/bonfire uncommon cooking—not appearance of warming cold—only forbidden where cooking could occur... First reasoning in Shulchan Aruch there soup cooled forbidden—Rosh establishes Mishnah liquids regarding dry food strained from “lest boil” decree—Rashi Rashba no contradiction—lest boil on bonfire/kirah—similar cooked dish Rosh likewise—not forced.
But to insulate—even fully cooked no cooking-after-cooking still forbidden hatmanah—siman 257 sk 7 wherever we forbid… ch.3 shehiyah dispute but hatmanah unanimous—forbidden here too.

Likewise forbidden… they did not permit—only fully cooked return permitted yet needs all conditions return specifically even shrinks harmed specifically return from Shabbat 37b Rabbi Oshaya even without cooking as above.
Provided—as above.
Some dispute here if…—as Tosafos say likewise.
And all matters—even rabbinic prohibition forbids telling non-Jew—as non-Jew who came to extinguish—even unnecessary.
And if he did so—even rabbinic prohibition forbids via non-Jew even after the fact—Beitzah 25a beyond boundary forbidden—all the more poskim who hold cooled soup biblical—not like Magen Avraham.
However if not—as sk 1 if non-Jew returned—even improves beautifully permitted although benefited since could eat without.

And after lighting then oven—no intent for pot—even pesik reisha only rabbinic—Kerisos 22 Yoma 34b double rabbinic—even rabbinic pesik reisha Beitzah 36 reasoning—even no trapping Shabbat 142b Rabbi Shimon agrees… telling forbidden rabbinic—even if himself Beitzah… non-Jew extinguisher 121a parallel—but telling with pesik reisha permitted—both lenient. Tosfos question pesik reisha only unwilling willing biblical Shabbat 103 Abaye Rava… great difficulty. Appears Rema did not rely on this—permits only if not completely cooled—therefore practice “therefore they are accustomed”—meaning such cases.
But via Israelite—Beitzah 34a “one who…”
Hot and cooked—as above sk 2.
